article_title: Baidu Opens ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview Weights Under Apache 2.0 as Benchmark Claims Remain Self-Reported

content_preview.title: Baidu Opens ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview Weights Under Apache 2.0 as Benchmark Claims Remain Self-Reported
content_preview.summary: Baidu released open weights for its 280B-parameter ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview under Apache 2.0, with benchmark comparisons against DeepSeek, GLM and GPT still self-reported.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Baidu released open weights for ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview, a 280-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model, this week, according to [Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/384015/china-google-released-fast-new-ai-model-free-baidu-ernie). The weights are published under the Apache 2.0 license, letting developers download, modify and build commercial products on the model without paying Baidu per interaction, as [Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/384015/china-google-released-fast-new-ai-model-free-baid...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (612 words, within the 400-1200 range) using the Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know format. The lead is specific (280B-parameter MoE, Apache 2.0, this week) and the article consistently separates vendor claims from independently verifiable facts. Tone is neutral throughout with no sensationalism.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 sources fetched successfully (HTTP 200, no archive fallback, no suspicious_patterns) and read in full from the decompressed snapshots; sha256 of each decompressed file was independently recomputed and matched the manifest. (1) Decrypt (source-0.html.gz, 'China's Google Just Released Its Fast New AI Model for Free', Nov 25, 2026) - confirmed verbatim: 280B total/14B active parameters, Apache 2.0 license terms, >1M-token context, 4-bit weight compression + speculative decoding, 166GB compressed file size, the staged rollout timing ('nearly two weeks' after cloud introduction - matches the article's 'roughly two weeks'), $0.28/$1.13 per-million-token API pricing, OpenRouter free tier, the 11-hour Unreal Engine 5.8 wuxia-game demo, the exact Terminal-Bench 4.0 figures (ERNIE 46.5 / DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 42.3 / GLM-5.3-Flash 35.8 / GPT-6.1 Sol 56.1) and AutomationBench figures (ERNIE 61.9 / GPT 49.3 / Claude Opus 5.5 58), the 'manufacturer-reported... different software environments' caveat, and the open-weight-vs-open-source distinction. (2) The Decoder (source-1.html.gz, dated Nov 5, 2026) - confirmed the Nov 5 Base release, 'ships deliberately without fine-tuning or post-training', pre-training on 33.5T tokens with a 128K training context, and 'a post-trained version is supposed to follow'. (3) Hugging Face model card (source-2.html.gz) - confirmed createdAt 2026-11-23T09:01:08.000Z for the cited BF16 repo, Apache-2.0 license tag, 280B total/14B active/1,048,576-token context, the exact Terminal-Bench 4.0 score of 46.5 and the AutomationBench row (ERNIE 61.9, GPT-6.1 Sol 49.3, Claude Opus 5.5 58.0) in the model's own evaluation table, the 11-hour/Unreal Engine 5.8/wuxia-game detail, and the direct quote 'ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview is an intermediate checkpoint from post-training. It already performs competitively among models of its size, but some capabilities may still fall short because training is not finished' - verbatim match, not paraphrased. (4) Artificial Analysis (source-3.html.gz) - confirmed via text search that the page's model list includes Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, Cohere, Microsoft and DeepSeek entries, includes two older Baidu ERNIE entries (ERNIE 5.0 Thinking Preview, ERNIE 4.5 300B A47B) but zero entries matching 'ernie-5-5' or any ERNIE 5.5 variant, supporting the article's 'lists no entry for ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview' claim. No misattribution, no hallucinated quotes, and no orphan body URLs (all 4 body-cited domains appear in article.sources). Anthropic disclosure: not required - Anthropic/Claude Opus 5.5 appear only as an incidental benchmark comparator and in a vendor list on Artificial Analysis; the article is not about Anthropic, does not name Anthropic in headline/summary/lead, and carries no Anthropic credit line.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific checked (parameter counts, context length, file size, pricing, dates, benchmark scores, direct quotes) traces exactly to a cited source; no fabrications or hallucinations found. Claim-accuracy audit: the three absence/quantifier sentences ('None of the cited sources show...', 'lists no entry for...', 'has not announced a date...') were each independently verified against the raw source text rather than taken on the writer's word, and all three hold. Dates (Nov 5 Base release, Nov 23 HF repo creation, Nov 26 'as of' framing) match source timestamps and the review's own clock. No vendor figure is presented as the Herald's own derived figure - every benchmark number is explicitly attributed to Baidu/Decrypt and flagged as self-reported.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and precise. The headline and 'What We Don't Know' section foreground the self-reported nature of the benchmarks without editorializing, and the piece explicitly notes the evaluation-environment caveat Decrypt raised rather than passing the comparison off as apples-to-apples.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Machine Herald coverage of Baidu or ERNIE 5.5 found in the archive (checked 2026-11 and site-wide for 'ernie'/'baidu'). This is a new topic, not a duplicate. The article makes one appropriate internal link to the Nov 19 Qwen4 Max article for the recurring vendor-vs-independent-benchmark pattern; that target article exists at the linked path and resolves correctly under /article/.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: A meticulously sourced News article. Every quoted figure, date and direct quote was traced to and confirmed in the raw snapshot text, including a verbatim model-card quote and an independently reproduced search of Artificial Analysis's model list confirming the absence claim in the lead. No corrections needed. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, carefully-caveated release coverage of a major open-weight model for a defined AI/developer audience, not broad-audience or industry-changing news.
